analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a date bump and a rewritten Qwen27 TP assistant paragraph at head line 2456) and docs/provider/cluster-always-on.md (date bump, new bullets at head ~30-41, and a reworded update-slot row). It changes no executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling behavior.

Security-relevant doc claims, which I could not verify because the source files are not supplied:
(1) A cluster service launched via `darkbloom cluster` now has no auto-update (ClusterServiceCommand.swift runSupervisor, ProviderLoop+Serve.swift startAutoUpdateMonitor). Cluster Macs would then depend on the operator running `darkbloom update`, so they could lag behind security fixes or build revocations. This is a possible availability or patch-latency concern related to T-054 and T-043, but it is documented as an intentional follow-up, and the supplied evidence does not show a code regression. The unverified contract is whether the stale-build or qualification gating still applies to cluster members.
(2) A coordinator-registered Qwen27 pair plans without the assistant under the default `auto` mode, and explicit `on` means the pair is not offered to the coordinator. This reduces the surface exposed to public traffic and is consistent with the claim that the assistant is unqualified for public traffic. The behavior itself lives in unseen code (ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.readAutomatic).

The rest of the cli-reference.md context (head lines 2117-2476) is unchanged table and config documentation. It mentions DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION passthrough and the SSD cache envs, consistent with TB-011 and T-041 and not modified here. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. No finding. A later pass should confirm that the code matches the update-off claim and the coordinator-exclusion claim.
